attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post, endorsed.

semantics.note: A faithful present-tense observation that OpenAI's consumer product loses billions. No period or measure is stated.

contract.note: Reading the claim as ChatGPT product-level losses in 2024, with at least $2B as 'billions', is a fair literal reading. But the period, the accounting basis and how shared costs are allocated are all the evaluator's choices. Requiring product-level accounts makes the claim hard to settle either way.

evidence.note: CNBC reports that OpenAI lost about $5B company-wide in 2024. That does not isolate the consumer ChatGPT product or allocate shared costs.

reviews.rationale: The contract requires product-level ChatGPT losses for 2024. The packet has only a company-wide loss figure of about $5B. That is consistent with the claim but cannot establish product-level losses under the contract's own measurement requirement. No evidence contradicts it. The evidence does not settle the outcome.

semantics.note: A causal allegation that Anthropic's prompting produced the reported blackmail. In LLM usage, 'prompting' can mean explicit instruction or deliberately engineering the input to elicit the behaviour. The speaker did not specify which.

contract.note: The contract adopts the narrow direct-instruction reading and admits that the result depends on it. In context, 'prompting' plausibly means engineering scenarios to elicit blackmail, which would favour the speaker. Picking the reading that defeats the claim is stretched against the speaker.

evidence.note: Anthropic's own disclosure says it gave no explicit instruction to blackmail. This bears only on the narrow reading, and it is a company statement about its own methods with no independent replication.
Anthropic's appendix admits it deliberately removed reasonable alternatives. This fits the broader elicitation reading but is also a company disclosure.

reviews.rationale: The result turns entirely on what 'prompting' means, and the speaker did not say. Under explicit instruction, Anthropic's disclosure cuts against the claim. Under deliberate elicitation, Anthropic's own appendix fits it. The contract's narrow reading is not a fair ordinary reading. Both sources are company self-disclosures, and 'so obviously' adds an opinion element. Not scored.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words, endorsed. In context, 'it' refers to OpenAI.

semantics.note: 'Will absolutely lower prices to compete' is a firm forecast with no deadline. It could also be read as describing ongoing behaviour, but a forecast is acceptable.

contract.note: Requiring an implemented cut on the same product plus credible evidence of competitive motive is a fair reading of 'to compete'. Mere passage of time cannot contradict the claim.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own announcement confirms cuts of 80% and 20% on existing models on 2026-07-30. This supports only the price-cut element; the stated motive is efficiency.
A secondary summary of WSJ reporting from June 2026 says cuts were being considered in anticipation of Anthropic. It does not tie the later implemented cuts to that motive.
The Decoder says competitive pressure 'likely' played a role, which is speculative. It does not establish motive.

reviews.rationale: A qualifying price cut was implemented after publication. But the packet gives no firm evidence that this cut was made to compete: OpenAI cites efficiency, and the reporting on motive covers only contemplated cuts or likely factors. The early-resolution rule is not met, and with no deadline nothing contradicts the forecast. Unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron states the figures in his own voice, without hedging. They likely restate reported projections, but he asserts them.

semantics.note: An unhedged statement about full-year 2025 revenue of about $12.7B and a loss of about $14B, made in mid-2025. Treating it as a forecast is reasonable.

contract.note: The 5% tolerance and the net-loss reading are evaluator-supplied but ordinary. The loss result is the same under any measure: net loss of about $39B, operating loss of about $20.9B and adjusted loss of about $8B are all far from $14B.

evidence.note: The FT, citing confirmed audited figures, reports 2025 revenue of about $13B, within 5% of $12.7B.
Ars reports a 2025 net loss of nearly $39B and an operating loss of about $20.9B. Both are far outside a $14B ±5% range.
The FT gives an adjusted loss of about $8B excluding non-cash charges. That is a different measure, and it is also far from $14B.

reviews.rationale: Calendar 2025 has ended. The revenue part holds: about $13B is within 5% of $12.7B. The loss part fails: net loss was about $39B, and no alternative measure (operating loss of about $20.9B, adjusted loss of about $8B) comes within tolerance of $14B. One component holds and one fails, so the result is mixed.
